title: valve operation
description: Isenthalpic throttle (Joule-Thomson let-down). Hardware-only: the single knob is the downstream pressure. A valve only DROPS pressure — it is a restriction, not a machine; to raise pressure use a pump for liquid or a compressor for gas. W = 0 and Q = 0 by definition, so the outlet temperature, the vapour fraction and the regime are RESULTS of an outer Newton on H_out = H_in at the new pressure (a hot liquid let down can flash). One combined outlet — the phases are NOT separated; chain a flash or drum downstream to split them. Tutorial credo01_valve_heater_drum.

P.title: Downstream pressure
P.description: Outlet (let-down) pressure. Must be below the inlet pressure — a valve can only drop pressure. T_out and the vapour fraction follow from the isenthalpic balance.
